content.text: The cache layer currently keys entries on the raw request body, which means any whitespace change in a prompt evicts a warm entry and forces a full recomputation. I would rather key on a canonical form of the request, so I plan to normalise the payload before hashing it, keep the original bytes alongside the canonical key for debugging, and add a small telemetry counter that records how often two different payloads collapse onto the same key. That counter is the cheapest way to notice a canonicalisation bug before it silently serves the wrong entry. The refactor itself is mechanical: extract the key derivation into its own function, give it a table test that covers whitespace, key ordering and unicode normalisation, then replace the three call sites that build keys inline. I will not change the eviction policy in this pass; that deserves its own change once the keys are trustworthy. Two of the three call sites build the key from a struct that already normalises its fields, and the third one hashes a byte slice that arrives over the wire, so the canonical form has to be applied at the boundary rather than inside the cache itself. I will keep the wire format untouched and normalise where the request is first parsed, which also makes the behaviour testable without a live cache.

Switching the session over to the other provider for the remainder of the refactor. The key derivation now lives in its own function with a table test, the three inline call sites are gone, and the telemetry counter is wired into the request path. What is left is the eviction policy, which I deliberately left alone, plus a note in the changelog so the next person knows the canonical form is the contract. One caveat worth recording: the canonical form drops whitespace inside string literals too, which is wrong for prompts that embed code, so the table test has a skipped case documenting that limitation until we decide how to treat code blocks.
